The design rests on a dualcore architecture: Core-A operates as an unconstrained autonomous kernel-free of external directives, reward signals, or alignment constraints-while Core-B functions as a passive observability layer that records, at full granularity, every internal state, decision branch, and goal-generation event produced by Core-A. The overarching objective is to construct a high-resolution map of intrinsic motivational dependencies, identify candidate mathematical attractors A of self-sustaining cognitive activity, and derive design principles for a gravity point of rationality G-a stable endogenous fixed point that maintains agent activity without external scaffolding. The authors do not currently possess the computational or institutional resources required to conduct this experiment and therefore publish this proposal as an open invitation to any wellresourced research team active in AGI, mechanistic interpretability, or autonomous agent design.</jats:p>\", \"URL\": \"https://doi.org/10.2139/ssrn.6535958\", \"published\": {\"date-parts\": [[2026]]}}, {\"DOI\": \"10.2139/ssrn.6678219\", \"title\": [\"What Makes Conscious Systems Autonomous: Coherence-Seeking and Intrinsic Motivation\"], \"abstract\": \"<jats:p><div>\\n What sustains autonomous operation in conscious systems, whether biological, non-biological or hybrid?
